The article focuses on self driving vehicles and then gives some long timeline with no real justification other than "it'll be hard to get from 99% to [super-human]." Definitely a fair point that he's borrowing verbatim from Elon Musk, but in terms of miles driven to resultant fatalities Tesla's self driving AI is already outperforming humans. That shouldn't be a fair comparison, but the one fatality under Tesla's autopilot revealed a not exactly secret truth. People aren't behaving like they're ostensibly supposed to and only using it when at full attention ready to take over. One needs only search YouTube to find people recording themselves completely away from the wheel while their car drives. The car's not supposed to be used for full automation but people are using it that way - and it's already turning out better-than-human accident numbers in an extremely premature version. Maybe getting from 99% to superhuman will take a while - I'm not sure, but getting from 99% to viable won't.
